title: Adjectives and Descriptions
definition: Adjectives describe people, objects, places, and feelings. In basic A1 sentences, adjectives after sein or werden do not take an ending: Das Haus ist groß. Adjectives placed directly before nouns can take endings, which are a later grammar step.

rules.title: Adjectives after sein
rules.explanation: After sein, the adjective normally stays in its basic form.

rules.title: Describe people
rules.explanation: Use common adjectives for appearance, personality, and feelings.

rules.title: Describe objects and places
rules.explanation: Adjectives can describe size, colour, price, age, and condition.

examples.german: Das Auto ist neu und schnell.
examples.english: The car is new and fast.

examples.german: Die Wohnung ist klein, aber schön.
examples.english: The apartment is small but beautiful.

rules.title: Opposites
rules.explanation: Learn adjectives in pairs to remember them more easily.

rules.title: Adjectives before nouns
rules.explanation: Before a noun, adjectives often take endings: ein großes Haus, eine schöne Wohnung. The ending depends on gender, case, and article; learn these patterns separately.

comparison.after_sein: Das Zimmer ist sauber. — The room is clean.
comparison.before_noun: Das ist ein sauberes Zimmer. — That is a clean room.

common_mistakes.explanation: After sein, the adjective has no ending.

common_mistakes.wrong: Der Kaffee ist heißer (when simply meaning hot).
common_mistakes.explanation: Use the base adjective unless you are making a comparison.

mastery_goal: You can describe people, things, and places with common adjectives in short A1 sentences.
